medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A student accepted into a medical school should expect to devote four years to pursuance of an MD degree. A student must maintain a regular rate of progress and demonstrate the capacity to handle the customary volume of academic work expected of a medical student. In cases of extenuating circumstances (medical / health problems, personal issues, financial issues) students may formally request  a Leave of Absence. The full policy and procedures for a Leave of Absence is available to all students in the Student Handbook found on the UCCOM Registrar page at http://med.uc.edu/registrar.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Over 65 student organizations and committees exist for medical students at the UC College of Medicine. This list grows annually to promote student involvement and inclusivity.  If a student feels there is an interest in a group that does not yet exist, s/he is encouraged to create a group (university funding is available).  Our MSA offers events and acts as a liaison between the student body and administration to ensure student rights and promote a healthy and collegial atmosphere. The student wellness committee offers a system of academic, social, emotional and psychological support to the students as well as events and a 24-hour student help line.  Peer mentoring, learning communities, and orientation activities ensure integration of wellness and professionalism topics into the student experience.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Cincinnati Medicine, founded in 1819, was the founding institution for the larger University of Cincinnati. The history and success of UC runs deep with over 200 years of training cutting edge physicians. We are the second oldest public medical school in the US and the oldest located west of the Allegheny Mountains. Located in a historic, urban neighborhood a mere 3-miles away from bustling downtown Cincinnati, UCCOM is positioned in the center of nationally ranked hospitals and clinics. The central location of the College and the fact that it is among the most consolidated in the nation (<.5 mi to clinical sites). Cincinnati, a robust, cosmopolitan city consists of over 2.2 million people in the metro area marking it as the largest metro area in Ohio and the 28th largest in the nation. Cincinnati is home to 9 Fortune 500 companies and 2 Fortune 100 companies, proving to be more economically diverse and strong than any other city in the region. Learn more at www.cincinnatichamber.com
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Medical students choose to live either in graduate housing (on-campus) provided through the University of Cincinnati or in non-campus housing near the medical campus. Off-campus housing ranges from walkable urban communities (0-10 minutes walk/bike/drive), to urban suburbs (10-15 minutes drive), to farther reaching suburbs (15-30 minutes drive). Cincinnati has been named the fifth most affordable metropolitan area to live in the US according to Forbes Magazine. Cost of living remains low and monthly rents range from $450-$900 depending on various factors.  Students primarily choose to live in the following Cincinnati neighborhoods: Avondale, Clifton, Corryville, East Walnut Hills, Hyde Park, Oakley, Mt. Adams, or Over The Rhine.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The University of Cincinnati College of Medicine Pride student group provides support to all individuals.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: The mission of the Student Wellness Committee (SWC) is to offer a system of academic, social, emotional and peer support to the students of UCCOM. The SWC comprises a faculty advisor and a committee of medical students. The SWC yearly wellness activities include exam stress relief and quarterly, informal social hours with UCCOM students, faculty and staff. An embedded counselor provides clinical support to UCCOM students as well as consultation and program development to faculty and staff. For more information visit: https://med.uc.edu/education/medical-student-education/wellness
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
The campus culture at the University of Cincinnati College of Medicine reflects a balance between academic rigor, collaboration, and a commitment to community engagement. Here are some key aspects of our culture:
- Collaborative and Supportive Environment
- Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion
- Innovation and Research Focus
- Community Engagement
- Dynamic Student Life
- Integration of Technology and Education
medSchoolStudLife.additionalSupportProgrameName: Career advising available for all students.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Students dress professionally in casual business attire considered suitable for a healthcare delivery setting. To view dress code examples, please visit med.uc.edu/registrar under Student Handbook.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Peer-to-peer tutoring by upper level medical students in all major science courses is provided for free. Individual appointments with the Assistant Dean of Academic Support are available.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students begin patient interaction in Year 1 through the Longitudinal Primary Care Clerkship which continues through January of Year 2. Students participate in elective shadowing experiences.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Years 1 and 2 offer student centered learning through hands-on laboratories, seminars, medical simulation, learning communities, a primary care clerkship, and team-based learning.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Years 1-2: Longitudinal Primary Care Clerkship. Year 3: Core Clerkships (Family Med, Neuro, Psych, Peds, Ob/Gyn, IM, Surgery) plus electives. Year 4: Acting Internships, IM electives, Intensive Clinic
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: Grading is a hybrid system.  In Years 1-2, students are graded on a Pass/Fail basis. Subsequently, in Years 3-4, a quartile system is employed for stratifying students within their class.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Some lectures are required. Students may view lectures using an electronic lecture capture system (e.g., streaming or podcast). Lectures involving clinical faculty or patient content are mandatory.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: Our integrated curriculum offers an innovative teaching and learning that prepares students for practice in the 21st century. We provide a dynamic learning environment with a focus on evolving societal needs, changing health care practice, and scientific advancements. For more than 5 years our students have engaged in a competency-driven curriculum, fully integrated across all 4 years. Years 1-2 offer student centered learning through hands-on labs, seminars, medical simulation, learning communities, a primary care clerkship, and team-based learning. Students complete BLS Training at Orientation and begin an 12 month Primary Care Clerkship between years 1 and 2. In Year 3, students rotate through 7 core clerkships and explore career options via specialty clerkships of their choosing. In Year 4, students refresh basic science knowledge and choose from over 100 primary care and specialty electives in nationally ranked programs within our Academic Health Center.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Medical students have the opportunity to explore and participate in primary care through the Longitudinal Primary Care Clerkship in their first and second years. Students are assigned to a primary care physician practice in January of their first year and work with that physician two-half days a month until the winter of second year. Students also have opportunities in primary care through student interest groups (Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Pediatrics), the Medical Student Scholars Programs (MSSP), service-learning opportunities such as the Urban Health Project, summer research in primary care, and shadowing experiences. In the third and fourth years of medical school, students have clinical rotations in each of the primary care disciplines which include two mandatory Acting Internships.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: We are a Clinical and Translational Science Award (CTSA) institution and provide a robust research environment that emphasizes excellence in basic, translational and clinical research.  A top-40 medical school for research, in 2019 our annual NIH fiscal-year dollar amount of peer review research funds granted to UC and our affiliated hospitals totaled more than $200 million with 686 individual grants that were received by nearly 450 principal investigators. Classified highly by the Carnegie Commission and ranked by the National Science Foundation as one America's top 25 public universities for federal research expenditures, we offer a wide range of world class research and training programs with premier institutes in cancer, diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular disease, neuroscience, heart/lung/vascular, and integrative health research. Medical students have access to paid research internships and volunteer research opportunities throughout our academic medical center.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Service is not required, we are proud of being a top service-focused medical school in the nation. Each year, 80% or more of of enrolled students participate in service.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: UC is a tier-one research, Clinical and Translational Science Award (CTSA) institution. Nearly 450 investigators receive almost 700 grants. Research is conducted by more than 500 faculty and students.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Cincinnati Children's, Cincinnati VA, Christ Hospital, Drake Ctr, Good Samaritan Hospital, Hoxworth Blood Ctr, Jewish Hospital, Lindner Ctr., Shriner's Hospital, UC Medical Ctr, West Chester Hospital
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: UCCOM uses a hybrid grading system meant to promote class cooperation. In Years 1-2, grading is Pass/Fail. In Years 3-4, grading is Pass/High Pass/Honors with a  cumulative quartile ranking.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Cincinnati Medicine recently celebrated its 200-year Bicentennial!  As the second oldest public medical school in the US, Cincinnati Medicine has provided superb clinical and teaching experiences with outstanding research facilities since 1819. Our nationally ranked teaching and research facilities are among the largest single-site health campuses in the US, with most clinical and research sites located within 0.5 mile radius of the College. The CARE/Crawley Building totals 240,000 square feet & is primarily dedicated to education and basic science laboratories.  Connected to our college of medicine is the 1 million-square-foot Medical Sciences Building research facilities. Graduates, ranked as highly competitive by national residency program directors, choose careers in a broad range of primary care and sub-specialty areas. Extensive research opportunities are available for medical students, residents, and fellows across a broad range of institutions in our academic health center.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: We work together in a spirit of collaboration, inclusion, and service: To educate and train the physicians, scientists, and health professionals of tomorrow; To advance knowledge through impactful, innovative research; To improve health and well-being through compassionate, patient-centered care.
medSchoolInformation.programUndergradCollege: Any undergraduate program at the University of Cincinnati
medSchoolInformation.programAbout: The Connections Dual Admissions Program, a BS/MD program, allows high school seniors to apply and be accepted to the University of Cincinnati undergraduate college and the University of Cincinnati College of Medicine simultaneously. The program attracts mature and intellectually curious students who are focused on service. The program is designed for students interested in health disparities, from a community engagement perspective, who are serious about a career in medicine.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Letters of recommendation must be processed through AMCAS.  Letters sent directly (not via AMCAS) will not be considered. It is the applicant's responsibility to inform recommenders of the proper protocol.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: The University of Cincinnati College of Medicine does not have a requirement on who letters should come from so we will leave this up to you regarding who you believe is best suited to write your letters, but we do encourage at least one (1) reference is able to speak to your clinical abilities and experiences.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Our redesigned interview approach combines technology and personal connection to thoroughly assess candidates while respecting their time. The process features a comprehensive six-station asynchronous virtual interview (through Kira Talent), followed by a focused one-on-one virtual meeting with a faculty member. This structured yet flexible format allows candidates to showcase their skills, experiences, and potential contributions to our institution while providing our faculty the opportunity to address specific questions and evaluate mission fit.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: Interview invitations are extended beginning in August.  Interviews will occur August through February.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Interviews will be conducted in a 2-part modality. Applicants will interview through Kira Talent (6 scenarios) and will receive an invitation for a 1:1 interview, as well.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Applicants who are AMCAS verified and who broadly meet holistic admissions criteria.
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: For more information regarding Cincinnati Medicine's Early Decision Program please visit https://med.uc.edu/admissions/medical-student-admissions/how-to-apply/early-decision-program(edp)
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: Cincinnati Medicine does not accept applications from international applicants (applicants must be US citizens/permanent residents). A special connection to Ohio is not required.
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: In-state tuition after yr 1. Tuition reciprocity for veterans, students with spouse working full-time in OH, residents of KY & IN who qualify: https://www.uc.edu/about/registrar/personal-info-changes

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Pass/Fail Coursework – The University of Cincinnati College of Medicine uses a holistic review and has no prerequisite courses (i.e., prerequisites are typically courses for which a letter grade is required by other programs). Since we do not have any prerequisite course requirements, we have no singular recommendation or policy for applicants regarding the impact of a pass/fail or letter grade on their candidacy. 
 
It is our recommendation that each applicant speak with their major advisor (and pre-professional advisor, if applicable) to discuss the manner in which a pass/fail or letter grade would impact their candidacy. In this way, an applicant can make a fully informed decision about how to move forward based upon the entirety of her/his/their application. We are confident that an applicant’s knowledgeable advisors can assist her/him/them in holistically considering the impact of this decision on the applicant’s medical school candidacy as a whole.

**General Admission Policies and Information**
Cincinnati Medicine is committed to a holistic review of applicants at every stage of the admissions process. The Admissions Committee does not use a formula as a basis for any interview or admissions decision, and all applicants receive consideration. 

To assess the applicant's readiness for medical school, the Committee on Admissions looks carefully at the following in making their determination: 

   A.  Academic background—grades and grade trends, all MCAT scores, postbaccalaureate and/or graduate experiences, honors courses, research experiences and any independent study courses.

   B.  Personal Growth and Development—maturity, integrity, leadership skills, empathy and interpersonal skills, involvement in activities helping others, exposure to diverse circumstances and settings, critical thinking skills, communication skills, and distance traveled (i.e., where the applicant has come from to where s/he/they are now).

   C.  Professional Development—understanding of humanistic dimensions of medicine, exploration of medicine through physician shadowing, distance traveled, demonstrated experiences in health care and service-oriented settings, knowledge of medical school demands and pressures, research productivity, external vs. internal pressures to pursue a medical career.

Decisions are communicated as soon as possible. Applicants are notified if they are accepted, placed on the Alternate List or denied acceptance within approximately two to four weeks.  Accepted applicants are required to respond to their Cincinnati Medicine offer within two weeks. The University of Cincinnati abides by the AAMC Traffic Rules and students may hold multiple acceptances until the stated date per the AAMC. After that date, students may only hold one medical school acceptance. 

Additional information about Cincinnati Medicine, our MD program and our Admissions process can be found at www.med.uc.edu ,  www.med.uc.edu/medicalstudentadmissions and www.med.uc.edu/mdadmissions
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: Our admissions committee reviews all MCAT scores submitted through the AMCAS application. Each set of scores is considered in context, and the committee evaluates an applicant’s complete testing history as part of the overall review process.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Community college coursework credit is accepted.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Letters of Intent are not expected nor required. Updates, notice of significant updates or achievements should be uploaded to the application portal, MedOneStop.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Applicants are strongly encouraged to review the most current Technical and Health Standards prior to applying. These standards outline the essential abilities and attributes required for matriculation, progression, and graduation from medical school. Please refer to the official website for the most up-to-date information.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The Office of Student Financial Services provides counseling to help each student fund their medical education and make sound financial decisions. Annually the College awards over $2 million in institutional aid in the form of merit-based scholarships, need-based scholarships, and low interest loans. Each year approximately 80% of our students receive some form of institutional (merit- or need-based scholarships or grants) or federal aid (student loans) or a combination of the two. Accepted applicants who complete the financial aid application process before March 1st will receive an estimated award letter in March. To receive consideration for need-based aid, applicants must submit the FAFSA with parental information. Further information and detailed instructions are available at  www.med.uc.edu/financialservices
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Tuition at the University of Cincinnati College of Medicine is determined annually by the Board of Trustees of the University. The College encourages the Board to keep tuition increases at a minimum, and we are pleased to offer our students one of the lowest rates in the region. Tuition rates are assessed by state residency status. Non-Ohio residents can apply to reclassify as Ohio residents for purposes of tuition assessment after 12 months of self-supporting residence in the state and in accord with university guidelines. As a result, historically the vast majority of our students have paid in-state rates for years two through four. Residents of Kentucky and selected counties in Indiana also may apply for reciprocity and metropolitan rates. Details on all state residency programs can be found at  www.uc.edu/registrar/residency.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
The University of Cincinnati College of Medicine's commitment to diversity includes prioritizing diversity of thought. Accordingly, all majors are valued and we have no specific course requirements. 

Students are expected to engage in a rigorous academic program grounded in the basic principles of the sciences fundamental to medicine and the psycho/social nature of humans. To succeed within this program, it is strongly recommended that applicants have the knowledge usually obtained in one-year courses in biology, general and organic chemistry (with labs), physics and biochemistry.

Highly competitive applicants have completed coursework in the social, cultural and behavioral sciences. All applicants should have acquired effective learning, communication, teamwork and problem-solving skills.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: The University of Cincinnati College of Medicine does not require prerequisite coursework.  Please see below for a list of coursework that is RECOMMENDED, but NOT required.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Applicants' materials are reviewed holistically and in their entirety. Invitations to interview are based on applicants' academic and personal characteristics, service experiences, and medically-related exploration. Applicant course selections are reviewed in detail; postbaccalaureate and graduate coursework will be considered. All MCAT administrations taken within the three years preceding matriculation are considered; it is preferred that applicants have 2 or fewer MCAT administrations. MCAT administrations are not necessarily averaged and we do not use superscoring.  In selecting students, the University of Cincinnati College of Medicine emphasizes critical thinking, personal motivation, maturity, coping skills, interpersonal skills/teamwork, and sensitivity and tolerance toward others. Students are admitted regardless of age, religion, gender, sexual orientation, race, color or national origin.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Applicants are strongly encouraged to engage in direct clinical experience to demonstrate meaningful exploration of the medical profession and an understanding of patient care environments. Physician shadowing can also serve as valuable clinical exposure. Both direct clinical experience and shadowing are reviewed equally as evidence of sustained interest in medicine and informed career exploration.
